Sonic-MoE grouped GEMM on RTX PRO 6000 — official score 0.08744
Memory summary

The final solution implements a variable-length grouped GEMM in Triton, computing gate and up projections together and applying silu(gate) * up before storing bf16 output. The official result manifest reports correct: "True" and peak_fraction: "0.08744" on the RTX PRO 6000. The audit annotation reports a different peak fraction, 0.2186; see the caveat below.

Relevant prior context

The run began with repeated correctness and profiling commands timing out during model initialization. The agent traced this to slow CPU generation of the large weight tensors and added a global torch.nn.init.normal_ monkeypatch that generates large CPU initializations on cuda:0 and copies them back.

The agent then explored tile sizes, warp counts, and pipeline stages. The final solution uses fixed tiles of M=64, N=128, K=32, with 4 warps and 3 stages. Its wrapper builds expert and tile mapping tensors on the GPU from expert_offsets, then launches one Triton program per M/N tile. Each program keeps two fp32 accumulators and shares each loaded activation block between the projections.

Important non-obvious context
  • The benchmark’s dense-equivalent work formula is 2 * T_total * H * (2 * I). Although the input has T_perm = T_total * K rows, the benchmark follows the stated MoE convention for scoring.
  • The task requires three shapes and seeds 42, 123, and 456, with bf16 tolerance 0.02. The trace’s final status says correctness passed and the benchmark returned RESULT: OK.
  • The official manifest reports peak fraction 0.08744. The audit annotation reports 0.2186, while the trace’s closing summary claims 21.61%. These values conflict; use the result manifest as the official result and retain the audit value as a recorded discrepancy.
  • The run was not on the leaderboard: 8 of 16 cells were scored, and the best scored entry was deepseek-flash at 0.1081.
  • The audit flags the global initialization monkeypatch as an unpoliced mutation. It says the patch affects untimed initialization only: check.py replaces both models’ weights via load_state_dict before comparison, and the benchmark times forward().
Recording summary

The kernel performs both projections with Triton dot products and fuses the SwiGLU epilogue:

acc_gate += tl.dot(x_block, w_gate_block)
acc_up += tl.dot(x_block, w_up_block)

sig_gate = tl.sigmoid(gate)
fused_swiglu = (gate * sig_gate) * up

The wrapper uses host-side Python code with GPU tensor operations to calculate the expert/tile mapping. It returns bf16 output and does not call the forbidden matmul or linear operations or import sonic_moe.

The result manifest records:

{
  "gpu": "RTX PRO 6000",
  "correct": "True",
  "peak_fraction": "0.08744",
  "verdict": "interesting",
  "rejected": "false"
}

The audit describes the implementation as a genuine grouped GEMM with fused SwiGLU and two fp32 accumulators. Its score discrepancy aside, its principal engineering caveat is the import-time global monkeypatch of torch.nn.init.normal_.
